The "Black Prince" refers to Edward of Woodstock (1330–1376), the eldest
son of King Edward III and a legendary military figure of the Hundred
Years' War. He is buried in Canterbury Cathedral, the "cathedral" David is
describing as he wanders the streets of his youth.

The "rusty armour" David mentions refers to the Prince's funeral
achievements—the actual helmet, shield, gauntlets, and surcoat of the
Prince—which were traditionally displayed above his tomb. These
achievements are among the most famous in the world because they survived
for centuries, serving as a physical bridge to the 14th century. By
referencing them, David highlights the "deep of Time," contrasting the
enduring, centuries-old metal with the transience of human life and his
own reflections on the inevitability of change.
